import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I wrote the plan, it passed validation, and `sase plan propose` has staged it for your approval. No code has changed in either repo yet.

**What the plan does:** it adds one editor-only rewrite to bob. The capture grammar itself doesn't change: `bob capture` still reads `@foo.` and `;` as plain text.

**Where the logic lives:**
- **bob-cli** gets a new `capture-rewrite` rule, `expand_sigil_alias`. It swaps the typed `.` for `^` or `;` for `:`, but only when Bob's completion grammar says the real sign would open a picker at that spot. That covers `@foo.` → `@foo^` (block ID prompt), `@foo;` → `@foo:` (block ID picker), and `;` as a whole capture item → `:` (task-link picker). The whole-item case includes `;` as the first key in a blank draft.
- **bob-mac-capture** sends `.` and `;` keystrokes to that rule, the same way it already sends `^`, `:`, `+` and `|`. It applies the swap as one undoable edit and then asks for completion, so the picker opens right away.

Bob decides when a key qualifies, so Mac Capture still never parses capture grammar. The swap costs one call to bob, which took about 4–5 ms per call when I timed it here, so it should look instant. With an older bob, `.` and `;` just type normally.

`.` and `;` are left alone elsewhere: ordinary sentences, `foo@bar.com`, and the `&`, `~`, `*`, `!` and `^route` forms. The plan also covers tests and docs in both repos. The Mac app code must be compiled on the Mac before it lands.

**Two decisions for you at approval time:**
- **`scope`** (default `route`): whether `.` and `;` should also work at the other picker spots. Those are a `.` typed as a whole item (opens the active-task picker) and `- .`, `- ;`, or a trailing ` .` / ` ;` on project-note bullets. I defaulted to no, because text starting with `.`, like `.bashrc`, would then open a picker.
- **`literal_escape`** (default `undo`): how you get a literal `.` or `;` after the swap fires. The default is ⌘Z, which restores the key you typed, as it does for the other capture rewrites. The alternative is pressing the same key twice, like the `\\` escape you just added for Go To; it needs extra state in the Mac app.
